standard.title: Explore language and culture connections
standard.description: explore connections between language and culture
standard.prior_knowledge: Foundation students bring lived experience of their home culture and language — cultural practices, celebrations, family routines and community contexts where the target language is used. They have not yet been asked to examine the connection between language and culture explicitly, nor compared their own cultural experiences with others' in a school context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore connections between the target language and the cultures in which it is used, identifying cultural practices, values and contexts associated with the language and connecting these to their own experience.

nodes.label: Recognising that language is used in cultural contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise that the target language is used in specific cultural contexts — communities, countries, everyday practices — and connect this to their own experience.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one context (community, country, family setting, celebration) where the target language is used, and make a connection to their own experience of that context.
nodes.typical_width: Explore the cultural contexts in which the target language is spoken — countries, communities in Australia and around the world, family and community settings; connect these to students' own experiences of language and culture; use maps, images and cultural artefacts to support exploration.
wider: Identify and compare different communities or countries where the target language is spoken — notice that the same language is used in different cultural settings with some variation
Connect the target language to First Nations Australian language contexts — notice that Australia is a multilingual country with many languages associated with different communities and places
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that language is embedded in cultural context is the conceptual entry point for all subsequent exploration of language-culture connections. Students who treat the target language as a set of phrases without cultural grounding cannot engage meaningfully with the cultural practices, values and identity questions that this descriptor and the broader strand address.

response_modes.reason: Cultural context awareness is built through encounter with varied examples — maps, stories, images, cultural artefacts, family connections. Background learners bring their own context but may not have framed it as a language-culture relationship. Multiple concrete contexts, including students' own, make the connection visible.

success_criteria: Can name at least one community, country or setting where the target language is used
Can make a personal connection to that context — for example, identifying a family member, community event or place associated with the target language

nodes.label: Exploring cultural practices through language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify cultural practices, celebrations or everyday routines associated with the target language and explore how language is used in these contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one cultural practice or celebration associated with the target language and describe how language is used in that context — for example, a greeting, wish or expression used on a specific occasion.
nodes.typical_width: Explore cultural practices, celebrations, stories, songs and everyday routines associated with the target language community; identify specific language used in these contexts; compare cultural practices with their own experience and with what they know of other communities.
wider: Participate in or reflect on a cultural practice and identify the language associated with it — for example, a greeting ritual, a celebration phrase, or a food-sharing custom
Compare a cultural practice from the target language community with an equivalent practice in another community — identify where the practices and associated language are similar or different

response_modes.reason: Cultural practice exploration at Foundation level works through accumulation — students build their sense of language-culture connection through multiple encounters with songs, stories, celebrations and routines. Single examples tend to be treated as curiosities. Varied cultural encounters build the repertoire from which the general insight emerges.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners bring authentic cultural knowledge that peers may not share. Width investment here — tasks that invite students to draw on and share their own cultural experience of the language — activates this knowledge and builds cultural confidence alongside linguistic awareness.
success_criteria: Can identify at least one cultural practice or occasion associated with the target language
Can describe at least one piece of language — a greeting, phrase or expression — used in that cultural context

nodes.label: Connecting own identity to language and culture
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on their own experience of language and culture, identifying ways in which the target language is part of their own identity and everyday life.
nodes.minimum_width: Share at least one way the target language is part of their own life — a family practice, a community connection, or a language used at home — using target language or English.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on the role of the target language in their own identity and daily life — family, community, celebrations, language use at home; share personal connections with peers; explore how people can belong to more than one language and cultural community simultaneously.
wider: Create a simple personal artefact — a drawing, caption or bilingual label — that represents their own language and cultural identity
Compare their own multilingual experience with a peer's — notice that different people have different language histories and cultural connections, and that this is a normal feature of Australian life

response_modes.reason: Personal identity reflection integrates the cultural context (node 1) and cultural practice (node 2) exploration into a personally grounded connection. The teaching investment is in creating a safe, inviting context where students can share their own language history — this is the moment where abstract cultural awareness becomes personally meaningful.

success_criteria: Can articulate at least one personal connection to the target language — a family, community or home context
Can identify themselves as a user of the target language in at least one context of their own life
